title: Reliability-first Sell Sheet / Battlecard — Platform Teams (Q4 iter B)
content:
PURPOSE
Quick internal sell-sheet + battlecard for conversations with Platform/Infra buyers where reliability, predictable latency, and graceful degradation are primary buying signals. This is intentionally concise — meant for AE/SE prep before a 30–45m call.

AUDIENCE
- Platform engineering leads, infra platform teams, SRE managers at midmarket/enterprise
- Pre-commit stage: they have an internal ML/LLM pilot or are standardizing inference across teams

ONE-LINER (openers)
- "'We help platform teams make LLM inference predictable and resilient across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments — focused on latency SLAs, cost predictability, and built-in fallback behavior.'"

TL;DR SELLING POINTS (elevator)
- Predictable latency: SLA options + routing policies that prioritize low-tail latency.
- Graceful degradation: automatic model fallbacks and region routing keep apps online during incidents.
- Observability: token-level cost/latency breakdowns and per-route tracing to find hot-spots.
- Deployment flexibility: hosted for speed, dedicated for predictable capacity, private for compliance.

PAIN SIGNALS TO LISTEN FOR
- 'We see enormous variance in p99 token latency depending on traffic patterns.'
- 'We built a prototype but can't hit production SLOs without significant infra work.'
- 'We need model access but can't expose data or outsource to unmanaged endpoints.'
- 'Costs spike unpredictably at peak and we don't know where to optimize.'

VALUE PROPS / EVIDENCE (short bullets)
- Routing + fallback: route by latency/cost/region; auto-fallback to quantized or smaller model variants when heavy tail occurs.
- Caching & batching: prefix & KV caching plus continuous batching reduces per-token cost while meeting SLOs.
- Kernel selection & quantization: runtime picks optimal kernels and quantization profile per workload to balance latency and token quality.
- Observability: per-request traces, token cost breakdown, and regression alerts tied to prompt sets.
- Contracts: Dedicated/reserved options for predictable throughput and enterprise SLAs.

PROOF POINTS (numbers to cite)
- Typical p95 improvement when enabling prefix caching: 20–40% (internal benchmark; varies by workload).
- Customers reporting 30–60% unit-cost reduction after applying Optimize recommendations + quantization.
- SLA-backed uptime for Dedicated customers: 99.9% (example; confirm for specific contract).

QUICK DEMO SCRIPT (5–7 min highlights)
1) Start: show Console route dashboard -> p50/p95/p99 splits for a route.
2) Show a tail event (simulated): switch to model variant fallback logs and show traffic shift -> demonstrate no request failures.
3) Open Optimize recommendations: show batching suggestion and projected cost delta.
4) Finish: Show audit log/KMS integration in Private deployment config (if customer cares about data residency).

OBJECTIONS & SUGGESTED RESPONSES
- "We can self-host and get better control." -> Acknowledge: self-host gives control but small ops teams pay enormous hidden costs. Redwood provides private deployments (VPC/on-prem) + ops playbooks AND a runtime optimized for inference kernels; we offload a lot of operational burden while keeping control.
- "Latency spikes are due to our app, not inference." -> Ask: can we show traces? Redwood's tracing can correlate app -> inference latencies to help isolate. Suggest a short proof-of-value: 2-week telemetry ingest of a single route.
- "Pricing is opaque / token billing hard to predict." -> Point to per-route token breakdown and Optimize toolkit which projects unit economics after tuning batching/cache/quantization. Offer example customerized model: we can run a short cost-sensitivity analysis.

PRICING / PACK GUIDANCE (for AE flows)
- Start with Hosted + Optimize trial (free credits) for early eval.
- If predictable high throughput: recommend Dedicated with a 3–6 month ramp and a baseline reserve.
- For regulated customers: propose Private deployment + enterprise support.
- Note: include burst options to avoid throttling during spikes.

SHORT CASE SNIPPET (lifted from internal notes, anonymized)
- Customer: fintech midmarket platform team. Problem: unpredictable p99s during batch job peaks and compliance needs for user prompts. Outcome: moved critical routes to Dedicated + enabled caching; p99 reduced from ~700ms to ~320ms for core route, cost/unit down ~38%.

TALK-TRACKS (one-liners by persona)
- SRE/Platform lead: 'You get predictable SLOs + traffic-aware fallbacks so customer-facing features don't fail under load.'
- VP Eng / Head of ML infra: 'We provide a consistent API across hosted, dedicated and private — makes handoff to platform teams painless.'
- Security/compliance: 'Private control plane and KMS/HSM integrations keep keys and logs within your VPC.'

RED FLAGS / DEAL RISKS TO ESCALATE TO AE/SolutionEng
- Customer requires air-gapped on-prem with zero-external telemetry (need legal + infra compliance check).
- Heavy custom model architectures requiring non-standard kernels (route to applied-ml onboarding).
- Procurement wanting extensive indemnities — engage Legal early.

FAQ (quick win answers)
- Q: How do you handle model regressions?
  A: Rollouts support canary + A/B + automatic fallback to prior stable model; quality monitoring tied to eval suites triggers alerts.
- Q: How intrusive is the Private deployment install?
  A: We provide an ops bundle + deployment runbook; timeline varies (4–12 weeks typical depending on network/KMS).

OPEN QUESTIONS / TODOs (work-in-progress — AE/SE input needed)
- Confirm latest Dedicated SLA number and update proofpoint (OWNER: Liam).
- Add 1–2 anonymized quotes from customers focused on reliability (OWNER: Zara).
- Create a 1-page printable handout for field use (OWNER: Diego).
- Run a quick telemetry ingest playbook for the '2-week POC' and draft standard scope (OWNER: Priya).

NOTES TO SELF / SE ASIDE

- Consider adding 'comparison appendix' vs. 2 specific competitors (ask sales ops if allowed).

UNRESOLVED

- Need permission for including customer names / exact metrics in handouts.

END OF DRAFT
